title: Recordings with Armstrong and Hines: film, Switzerland, Paris and the Crescendo
summary: They go through the film 'New Orleans' music, a 1949 Empire Room broadcast, concerts in Switzerland and Trieste, Paris with Earl Hines and Buck Clayton, and the 1962 session; he only started keeping his records ten years ago.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: "Farewell to New Orleans, "Do you know what it means" and "Dippermouth Blues",.
Yeah, that's from that "New Orleans" picture.
And then most of your recording was with Louie.
Oh, the Empire Room, it says. March 1949. That must have been an Air check.
It must have been. I mean, there wasn't any actual recording session.
That's where I met you. It says (Inaudible) a radio. A Swiss concert and with Louie -- you went to Switzerland with Louie, with Concert du Suisse is that what is?
And then Earl Hines, Paris, with Buck Clayton, Barney Bigard, Arvell Shaw, and Wallace Bishop.
But that was without Louie? [on the recording date - 8.6.]
That was with Buck Clayton and Earl Hines.
Oh, then at the Crescendo with Louie again.
So you can see I did a lot of recording in my days.
Pages and pages, stacks and stacks of records.
Do you have most of the records you made?
I started, I only started getting my records about the last 10 years, maybe. I didn't bother with records before.
Oh, here's the one that you were telling me about, the 10th of April, 1962, Benny Carter, Ben Webster, Barney Bigard, Shorty Sherock, --
"Opening Blues," "Lula", "When Lights Are Low," "You Can't Tell the Difference" When the Sun Goes Down Blues.
And this goes up to 1968, or into 1968.
